questions.q: What is the correct order of the four strokes in an internal combustion engine?
options: Power, intake, compression, exhaust
Compression, intake, exhaust, power
Intake, compression, power, exhaust
Exhaust, power, compression, intake
questions.explain: The fixed order is intake (the mixture enters), compression (the piston rises and compresses it), power (ignition pushes the piston down) and exhaust (the gases leave).

questions.q: What ignites the air-fuel mixture on the power stroke of a petrol engine?
options: Contact with the crankshaft
The exhaust valve opening
A spark from the spark plug
Compression heat alone
questions.explain: In a petrol engine the spark plug creates a spark at the exact moment the vehicle’s computer decides, and that is what ignites the mixture.

questions.q: What is the camshaft’s job?
options: To cool the engine
To measure the engine’s rotational speed
To open and close the valves at the right time in every cycle
To drive the vehicle’s wheels directly
questions.explain: The camshaft, synchronised to the crankshaft by a timing belt or chain, opens and closes the intake and exhaust valves at the precise timing required.

questions.q: What does the red zone on the RPM gauge mark?
options: A fault in the oxygen sensor
The recommended speed for urban driving
The most economical speed to drive at
An engine speed you must not exceed, to avoid damaging its parts
questions.explain: The red zone marks an upper limit on engine revolutions per minute; above it, engine parts can be damaged.

questions.q: What is the main difference between ignition in a petrol engine and ignition in a diesel engine?
options: Petrol ignites with a spark from the spark plug; diesel ignites fuel injected into air made hot by compression, with no spark plug
There is no difference, both use a spark plug
Petrol does not need air at all
Diesel ignites with a spark; petrol ignites from compression heat alone
questions.explain: A diesel engine compresses air at a very high compression ratio until it becomes very hot, and then the fuel injected into it ignites by itself — with no spark plug.

questions.q: Why does a diesel engine need glow plugs on a cold morning?
options: To clean the particulate filter
To pre-heat the combustion chamber, because compression alone is not always enough in the cold
To ignite the fuel with a spark
To cool the engine before starting
questions.explain: In the cold, the air does not always heat up enough from compression alone. The glow plugs pre-heat the combustion chamber, and you wait for the glow plug light to go out before starting.

questions.q: What does the turbocharger do in an engine?
options: Compresses extra air into the cylinders, driven by the exhaust gases, to boost power
Only regulates the flow of fuel
Cools the coolant
Filters dirt out of the engine oil
questions.explain: The turbocharger is driven by the exhaust gases themselves and compresses extra air into the cylinders, which lets the engine burn more fuel and produce more power.

questions.q: What does the intercooler do?
options: Heats the air coming out of the turbocharger
Switches between a petrol engine and a diesel engine
Cools the compressed air from the turbocharger, so even more air can be compressed into the same volume
Filters soot particles out of the exhaust gases
questions.explain: Compressed air heats up. The intercooler cools it before it enters the cylinders, allowing denser air to be compressed into the same volume.

questions.q: What does engine oil do?
options: Replaces the brake fluid
Only cools the vehicle from the outside
Slides between moving parts, cools them and collects dirt and metal particles
Only cleans the windows
questions.explain: Engine oil forms a sliding film between moving parts, cools them and collects dirt and metal particles created by wear.

questions.q: What do you do when the oil pressure warning light comes on while driving?
options: Keep going carefully to the nearest garage
Accelerate to reach a petrol station faster
Ignore it, it is usually a minor fault
Stop immediately in a safe place and switch off the engine
questions.explain: Low oil pressure means the engine’s parts are barely protected. Stop immediately and switch off — continuing to drive can destroy the engine within minutes.

questions.q: What does the number in an oil viscosity grade such as 5W-30 describe?
options: The number of kilometres until the next oil change
How the oil flows when cold (the number before the W) and when hot (the number after)
The size of oil filter required
The number of litres the engine needs
questions.explain: The number before the W describes how the oil flows when cold, and the number after it describes how it flows when hot. Always use the grade the vehicle manufacturer specifies.

questions.q: When is it correct to check the engine oil level on the dipstick?
options: Right after a long drive, while the engine is hot
Only once a year
Timing does not matter
When the engine is cold, before driving
questions.explain: A correct oil level check is done when the engine is cold and has not been driven recently, so the oil has had time to drain into the sump and give an accurate reading.

questions.q: What is the thermostat’s job in the cooling system?
options: To stay closed until the engine reaches working temperature, and only then open flow to the radiator
To pump the coolant round the circuit
To run the cooling fan at full speed at all times
To lower the pressure in the cooling system
questions.explain: The thermostat stays closed while the engine is cold, so it warms up faster, and opens only once it reaches working temperature — only then does it let fluid flow through the radiator.

questions.q: Why must you never open a radiator cap while the engine is hot?
options: It will make the vehicle restart on its own
There is no real risk in doing so
The fluid is boiling and under pressure, and can erupt and cause severe burns
The cap is always locked and cannot be opened
questions.explain: The system is sealed and under pressure, which raises the boiling point. Opening the cap releases the pressure at once, and the boiling fluid can erupt.

questions.q: When does the cooling fan switch on?
options: Only at high speed on a expressway
Only when the engine is switched off
Never automatically
When natural airflow through the radiator is not enough, such as driving slowly or stopped
questions.explain: When driving slowly or stopped, natural airflow through the radiator is weak, so the fan switches on automatically to keep cooling.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a typical cause of overheating?
options: A faulty thermostat or water pump
A low coolant level due to a leak
A clogged air filter
A torn belt that drives the water pump
questions.explain: A clogged air filter hurts power and fuel consumption, but is not a typical cause of overheating. The others — a leak, a faulty thermostat or pump, and a torn belt — are.

questions.q: What does the air filter do?
options: Filters the fuel before it enters the tank
Cools the air entering the radiator
Stops dust and insects before they reach the cylinders
Filters dirt out of the brake fluid
questions.explain: The air filter stops dust and particles before the air reaches the cylinders. A clogged filter restricts airflow and hurts power and fuel consumption.

questions.q: What does the octane rating of petrol describe?
options: The amount of energy in a litre of fuel
The flow rate through the fuel pump
The number of litres in the tank
How well the fuel resists uncontrolled ignition (knocking)
questions.explain: The octane rating describes resistance to “knocking” — the mixture igniting by itself too early. Engines with a high compression ratio usually need a higher octane rating.

questions.q: You have filled a petrol vehicle with diesel by mistake. What do you do?
options: Also fill up with petrol, to dilute the diesel
Drive only at low speed until the wrong fuel runs out
Do not start the engine at all, and call roadside assistance to drain the tank
Start the engine and drive carefully to the nearest garage
questions.explain: The wrong fuel in the tank is a serious fault. Do not start the engine, so as not to circulate the wrong fuel through the system — call roadside assistance to drain the tank.

questions.q: What is the correct fuel path from the tank to the injectors?
options: Fuel pump → fuel tank → injectors
Fuel tank → fuel filter → fuel pump → injectors
Injectors → fuel filter → fuel tank
Fuel tank → air filter → injectors
questions.explain: Fuel leaves the tank, passes through the fuel filter, which cleans out dirt, and is drawn by the fuel pump under pressure to the injectors.

questions.q: What does the catalytic converter do?
options: Turns a large part of the harmful exhaust gases into less harmful ones
Traps soot particles in a diesel
Supplies electricity to the ignition system
Reduces exhaust noise
questions.explain: The catalytic converter turns a large part of the harmful gases into less harmful ones. Reducing noise is the silencer’s job, not the converter’s.

questions.q: What is “regeneration” of a diesel particulate filter (DPF), and when does it happen best?
options: A self-burn of the particles it has collected, which usually happens during sustained driving at a relatively high RPM
A manual clean-out that has to be done at a garage every week
Cleaning dust out of the radiator
An engine oil change
questions.explain: The particulate filter cleans itself from time to time in a controlled burn of the particles it has collected. Sustained driving, such as on a non-urban road, helps the process; short trips in town only can stop it from cleaning itself.

questions.q: The “check engine” light starts to **flash** while you are driving. What is right to do?
options: Accelerate to reach your destination faster
Ignore it — it is just as important as a steady light
Switch the engine off and on several times to “reset” it
Slow down, avoid hard acceleration and stop as soon as you can — there is a serious misfire that can destroy the catalytic converter
questions.explain: A flashing “check engine” light marks a serious misfire. Keep going carefully, avoid hard acceleration and stop as soon as you can, so as not to destroy the catalytic converter.

questions.q: What does the AdBlue (SCR) system do in modern diesels?
options: Cools the engine
Cleans the windscreen
Replaces the need for engine oil
Injects a urea solution into the exhaust gases to cut nitrogen oxides
questions.explain: The AdBlue system injects a urea solution into the exhaust gases to neutralise nitrogen oxides. The AdBlue tank needs topping up from time to time, separate from the fuel tank.
